SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
S.I. Special Branch/fffff,
REPORT
Date December, 13, 19 37

Subject Activities of Koo Vung-dau, former officer of the Jessfield
Branch of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau.
Made by D.I. Fen Lien-pih Forwarded by

It is reported that Koo Vung-dau(顧頌濤), a former
sub-inspector attached to the Jessfield Branch of the Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau, has been approached by the
managements of certain Japanese factories in the Western
District to act as their Chinese advisor and liaison officer.
It is learned that Koo Vung-dau has been recently engaged
in a "racket" whereby he undertakes to remove goods from
Chinese territory to the Settlement on behalf of the owners.
When approached to remove goods, a deposit of a sum of $20,
$50 and $100 is charged as a locomotion allowance, and is
assessed according to the value of the goods. Investigations
are then instituted as to the state of the place where the goods
are stored and should the place be found burned or the goods
stolen, the locomotion charge will not be refunded. Should
the place and goods be in good condition, they are removed,
but a further transportation fee equivalent to 20% to 30%
of the value of the goods is then charged, the first deposit
being incorporated in the charge.
The goods are transported to the Settlement and land
at two places on the Soochow Creek, either at Jessfield
Village or at jetties in the Louza district. If landing
in Jessfield Village, a pass is applied for from the Italian
Troops, who are defending that sector, but in case the
application is refused, arrangements are then made with the
Japanese military authorities for permission to allow the
junks to proceed to the Louza District, where the vessels
are unloaded. One named Hsu(許), a follower of Koo, is
said to be responsible for the transportation arrangements.
A few days ago Koo Vung-dau arranged the transportation

C.P.
DC (a)
(印：MB 12 DEC. 1937 JESSFIELD)
(印：PHILIP M SICKER 14 DEC. 1937 (CA))

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案编号............
S.I. 特别科/fffff，
报告
日期 1937年12月13日

主题：前上海市政府警察局极司菲尔路分局警官顾颂涛的活动。
制作人：督察芬连璧（Fen Lien-pih） 转呈人：

据报，前上海市政府警察局极司菲尔路分局副督察顾颂涛（Koo Vung-dau，顧頌濤），已受到西区某些日本工厂管理层的接洽，拟聘其担任华方顾问及联络官。据悉，顾颂涛近期从事一种“勒索勾当”，即代表货主将货物从中国辖区运入租界。在受理搬运委托时，根据货物价值收取20元、50元或100元不等的定金，作为“移动津贴”。随后会对货物存放地点的状况进行调查；若发现该地点被焚毁或货物被盗，则不予退还移动津贴。若地点及货物状况良好，则实施搬运，但此后会另行收取相当于货物价值20%至30%的运输费，此前的定金亦计入该费用之中。

货物被运至租界后，在苏州河的两处地点上岸，一处在极司菲尔村（Jessfield Village），另一处在罗家嘴（Louza）地区的码头。若在极司菲尔村上岸，需向防守该区域的意大利军队申请通行证；但若申请被拒，则会与日本军方当局安排，获准让舢板船前往罗家嘴地区卸货。据悉，一名姓许（Hsu，許）的顾氏追随者负责运输安排事宜。数日前，顾颂涛安排了

C.P.
DC (a)
（印：MB 1937年12月12日 极司菲尔路）
（印：PHILIP M SICKER 1937年12月14日 (CA)）

of three boatloads of potatoes from Nanziang to Shanghai,
which were unloaded at the Jessfield Village; also he further
arranged the transportation of three boatloads of bituminous
coal from Pootung, which were unloaded at the City Government
Ferry Pontoon, The Bund near Peking Road, and it is reported
a transportation fee of $100 per boat was charged for the
potatoes, and $200 for each boat of coal.
Further negotiations are in progress for the removal of
200 piculs of firewood from Zah Hwei Kong, Nantso, and also
the transportation of fish from inland places.

从南翔（Nanziang）向上海运输三船土豆，并在极司菲尔村卸货；此外，他还安排了从浦东（Pootung）运输三船烟煤，在北京路附近外滩的市政府轮渡浮码头卸货。据报，土豆每船收取运输费100元，煤炭每船收取200元。

目前正就从中市（Nantso）查惠公（Zah Hwei Kong，音译）运出200担柴火，以及从内地各处运输鱼类的事宜进行进一步磋商。
